Furthermore, Ford and ORNL can continue to advance the current 1 way coupling multiscale modeling scheme to the 2 way coupling macro-micro scheme, where the two scales will be run at the same time with the micro-model to be mobile and follow the path of crack propagation. 8. CONCLUSIONS This developed multiscale macro→micro←nano or MMN modeling approach is successfully used to obtain the correlations between material microstructure of different scale of AA6111 alloys and bendability in terms of crack initiation strain on the surface. A reduced order model (RPM) is hence obtained to relate the material nano-scale microstructure to its bendability, while assuming the submicron scale and meso-scale microstructure are similar and It was successfully used to predict the bendability of 6HS2-T6 and 6HS4-T6 alloys, but predicts higher crack initiation strain in the 6HS2-T4 and 6HS4-T4 alloys than DIC measurement. The reason of this deviation may be due to the different microstructure and properties of the material on the surface than that of the bulk, since the surface cracks does not connects and propagate through the thickness. 9.
